blockbuilder-explorer.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark theme with consistent panel styling and a visually striking color-usage scatter plot, but the force-directed graph is too dense to read (labels overlap badly) and the histogram is generic steelblue with no typographic or color refinement.
blockbuilder-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Strong encoding integrity: scaleSqrt used correctly for node and color-point radii in both the network and scatter views, bar chart baseline is zero with domain derived from d3.max, and the fixed hue/lightness axes [0,360]/[0,100] are semantically appropriate rather than arbitrary — only minor concern is the foreground-bar y-scale is frozen to the full-dataset max, which is a deliberate design choice that works correctly here.
flags: Update Storm (partial): bitFilter.set() iterates 34K records synchronously on every brush mousemove event before the RAF-coalesced render — CPU computation is un-throttled even though DOM mutations are deferred
blockbuilder-explorer.stress_test_note: Dirty-flag + RAF pattern correctly coalesces renders, pointer events prevent mouse-touch fights, no D3 transitions to interrupt, and no cross-view dispatch loops; only weakness is expensive synchronous bitFilter.set() computation running un-throttled inside brush and color-brush drag handlers.
blockbuilder-explorer.cognitive_load_note: 4-view crossfilter with clear top-to-bottom filter→results flow; 60-node network is pre-computed and static (not live force reheat) with labels on top 15 reducing hairball risk, but the color scatter's ~35k unlabeled dots require interaction to extract meaning from the dense hue×lightness cloud.
